hyps.why: Filling an empty edge 3 can complete the input-output path, giving a huge gain, while replacing an existing op gives a small change.
Adding a conv on an absent edge 4 reconnects a disconnected cell, whereas replacing an existing op changes accuracy only slightly.
Edge 5 being none often leaves the output unreachable, so adding a conv yields a large jump (e.g. +76 C10).
A skip on an empty edge 3 restores connectivity to the output, a much larger effect than swapping ops.
A skip on an empty edge 4 restores the path (+78 C10 in a disconnected parent), unlike replacing an existing op.
Skip on a none edge 5 reconnects the output, giving a big gain versus the near-zero effect of swapping ops.
Any non-none op on an absent edge 5 completes the path and gives a large gain, unlike replacing an existing op.
Adding a parameter-free op on an empty edge 4 reconnects a broken cell, a far larger effect than swapping ops.
Filling an empty edge 3 with any conv restores the direct input-output path and has a bigger effect than replacing an existing op.
Removing a conv3x3 loses capacity and is neutral to harmful, whereas removing a parameter-free op like avg_pool can help.
